claim: IGNOU Unit 13 derives the multiplier from M = C + D (C currency, D demand deposits) and H = C + R (R reserves with banks); H is the 'high powered (reserve or base) money'; M/H = (cdr + 1)/(cdr + rr)
value: H = C + R; M = C + D
source: IGNOU, Economics optional, Unit 13 (The Financial Sector and Monetary Policy)
note: Same content as ECO16-T07; adds that M is C + demand deposits only (time deposits left out) and that H is C + R

claim: IGNOU's glossary: monetary base = currency in the hands of the public plus commercial bank reserves, 'also called high powered money'; the money multiplier gives the factor by which currency plus deposits change when the base changes
source: IGNOU, Economics optional, Unit 13 (The Financial Sector and Monetary Policy)
page_or_section: 13.7 Key Words, PDF p.22 (Monetary Base and Money Multiplier entries)
note: Definition for the 'describe' part. Quote 'also called high powered money' (5 words) | [Audit 11 Nov 2026] FIX: page added; quote verified.

claim: RBI's definition: Reserve Money (M0) = currency in circulation + bankers' deposits with RBI + 'other' deposits with RBI. The Reddy Working Group on Money Supply (June 1998) recommended four aggregates M0, M1, M2, M3 and kept the reserve money definition 'unaltered'
source: RBI Reports page, 'New Monetary Aggregates: an Introduction' (1 Jun 1998); ID 293 per ECO-16 search_log
note: Adds to ECO16-R08, R10. This RBI page does not itself discuss the H theory or the multiplier; the theory is read at IGNOU. claim: Higher reserve money in India: growth rate of reserve money 12.6% y-o-y on 31 Jul 2026 (ledger ECO16-I04); RBI Bulletin Jun 2022 says reserve money (base money) rose 28.2% and broad money 22.0% between Mar 2020 and Mar 2022, with the multiplier at 5.57 (2019-20) and 5.20 (2021-22)
source: RBI Bulletin, June 2022, 'Central Bank Balance Sheet Size and Inflation: Unravelling the Fuzzy Dynamics' (S. Pattanaik, B. B. Bhoi, H. K. Behera, RBI)
page_or_section: Section on money aggregates and nominal GDP; note 12
note: Shows H and M move with a changing multiplier. LEVEL of reserve money today: NOT FOUND (blocked, see 2024-ECO1-4A-08)

claim: RBI Bulletin Jun 2022 on the H-to-M link: money supply is determined endogenously by private-sector (and government) demand which the central bank accommodates; in shocks the link between reserve money and broad money breaks down
source: RBI Bulletin, June 2022, 'Central Bank Balance Sheet Size and Inflation: Unravelling the Fuzzy Dynamics' (S. Pattanaik, B. B. Bhoi, H. K. Behera, RBI)
note: Useful as the critique of the H theory's assumption that the multiplier is stable. RBI authors' view, not the RBI's policy statement

claim: Assumptions of the H theory as a list (cdr and rr stable; banks hold only a fixed desired excess reserve; H set by the central bank; M = C + demand deposits) are drawn by us from the IGNOU derivation (-01, -02) and glossary; no primary source read prints them as a numbered list
source: IGNOU, Economics optional, Unit 13 (The Financial Sector and Monetary Policy)
note: Present as 'assumptions in the derivation'. Each item traces to a row: ratios as given (-01), desired excess reserves (2024-ECO1-4A-04), exogenous H (ECO16-T08), M = C + D (-01). Note IGNOU says Ms is exogenous OR endogenous
